title: When the Hollow Wakes Anew
premise: Ulyana Coldharbour, a debt-bound scribe in the Ledger Guild of Vaskarand, discovers that the guild's 'impossible things' are fragments of a country called Ostmere that was erased from history two centuries ago — and that the child who arrives speaking its dead language is the last living heir of its royal line. As Ulyana transcribes the boy's memories into the ledgers, he learns the guild has been feeding those memories to something beneath the city: the Hollow, an entity that ate Ostmere and now stirs to finish its meal. To save the child, Ulyana must reconstruct Ostmere's true name from scattered ledger entries and open the one door out of a country that no longer exists. In the end, Ulyana pays his own accumulated memories as toll — forgetting his mother, his debts, and finally his own name — so the boy can walk through into a restored Ostmere, leaving Ulyana a blank page who must begin writing himself anew.
about_author: Rosalind Winterbourne is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the ledgers of defunct merchant guilds before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about paperwork, memory, and the quiet violence of institutions.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unpaid Ink
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. We meet him cataloguing impossible acquisitions — bottled thunder, a saint's second shadow — while calculating his ever-growing debt to the guild. A routine audit reveals an entry in his own handwriting he never wrote. Emotional beat: weary resignation sharpening into unease.

chapters.title: A Boy at the Loading Door
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. During a night inventory, a mud-caked child appears at the guild's loading door speaking a language no living tongue should know. The guildmaster orders him locked in the vault 'for appraisal.' Ulyana feels an inexplicable recognition. Beat: reluctant protectiveness awakening.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Vanished
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, with interleaved ledger excerpts. Researching the boy's language, Ulyana finds references to Ostmere — a kingdom struck from every map, treaty, and memory two hundred years ago, except in the guild's oldest books. Beat: vertigo of discovering a hole in the world.

chapters.title: What the Vault Keeps
chapters.summary: The boy's POV, fragmented and dreamlike. He remembers snow, a bell tower, a mother singing in the dead language — and a darkness that drank his city while everyone forgot it mid-scream. Beat: grief rendered as sensory memory.

chapters.title: Terms of Indenture
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The guildmaster offers Ulyana debt-forgiveness in exchange for transcribing the boy's memories into the master ledger. Desperate, Ulyana agrees without reading the full contract. Beat: hope curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: First Transcription
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The first session: as the boy speaks, ink moves on the page unbidden, and Ulyana feels the boy's memories as his own. He glimpses the Hollow — vast, patient, buried beneath the city. Beat: wonder laced with violation.

chapters.title: The Archivist Who Forgot Herself
chapters.summary: Senior archivist Maren's POV. Maren, once the previous transcriptionist, has forgotten her own daughter but remembers every ledger line. She warns Ulyana obliquely: the ledger doesn't record memory; it eats it. Beat: dread delivered with terrible tenderness.

chapters.title: Debts Written in Bone
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana investigates his own contract and finds his parents sold his future memory-rights at his birth — his whole life was collateral. The Hollow's hunger and the guild's lending are the same system. Beat: rage and betrayal.

chapters.title: The Bell That Rings Underwater
chapters.summary: The boy's POV. The boy begins remembering forward — things that haven't happened — including Ulyana opening a door. The guildmasters grow alarmed; the Hollow stirs beneath the foundations, and chandeliers sway to a soundless bell. Beat: prophetic terror.

chapters.title: An Inventory of Absences
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana and Maren secretly cross-reference erased pages and discover the guild founded itself on Ostmere's ruin — its capital literally built atop the drowned palace. Beat: the institution revealed as predator.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Confession
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Havel's POV. Havel reveals he was born in Ostmere's final hour, kept alive by feeding the Hollow memories so it sleeps. Feeding it the boy will buy another century. He believes this is mercy. Beat: chilling, sympathetic villainy.

chapters.title: A Door Out of Nowhere
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Deciphering the ledgers, Ulyana finds the escape route: Ostmere's true name, spoken whole, opens the original door — but the name was shattered across thousands of ledger entries and fed piecemeal to the Hollow. Beat: desperate hope with a mathematical problem.

chapters.title: Reassembly
chapters.summary: Dual POV (Ulyana and the boy). Working nights, they reconstruct fragments — the boy supplies what the ledgers lack, each word costing him more of himself. They fall into a fragile, sibling-like bond. Beat: love built from shared erosion.

chapters.title: Maren Pays Her Toll
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Caught helping, Maren is made to pay in memories — she chooses to keep the ledger knowledge and lose her daughter's face entirely. She leaves Ulyana a coded warning hidden in a marginalia. Beat: sacrifice as quiet heroism.

chapters.title: The Hollow Wakes
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. An earthquake of forgetting sweeps the city: citizens pause mid-sentence, names slip, streets rearrange. The Hollow is waking early because the boy's presence accelerates it. Beat: civilization unraveling at the edges.

chapters.title: Havel's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Havel locks down the guild for the final feeding. Ulyana realizes the assembled name is one syllable short — the missing piece is inside the Hollow itself, in the memory it took first: Ostmere's founding moment. Beat: cornered resolve.

chapters.title: Into the Drowned Palace
chapters.summary: Ulyana and the boy's POV, alternating. Descending through the guild's roots into the sunken palace, they walk corridors of crystallized memory, past petrified citizens mid-flight. Beat: awe and horror in equal measure.

chapters.title: The First Memory
chapters.summary: The boy's POV. At the palace heart, the boy touches the Hollow and receives Ostmere's founding memory — and learns the kingdom was born from a bargain with the Hollow originally; the monster and the country are the same wound. Beat: devastating revelation reframing everything.

chapters.title: The Price Named Aloud
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Cornered by Havel above and the Hollow below, Ulyana completes the name using his own most-cherished memories as the final syllables — offering them willingly rather than having them taken. Beat: agency seized from despair.

chapters.title: When the Hollow Wakes Anew
chapters.summary: Climax, multiple POVs. The name spoken, the door tears open; the Hollow rises not to devour but to be witnessed — Ostmere's erasure acknowledged at last. Havel, offered passage, chooses to stay and feed the Hollow his own long life, ending the cycle. Beat: catharsis through recognition.

chapters.title: A Kingdom Reassembled
chapters.summary: The boy's POV. Through the door lies Ostmere restored — not resurrected people, but a land that remembers itself, where the boy can grow up among ghosts made gentle. He looks back once. Beat: bittersweet homecoming.

chapters.title: Blank Page
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Memory spent, Ulyana wakes in the guild ruins with no name, no debts, only a ledger and a pen and muscle-memory of kindness. He writes the first line of a new book: his own. Beat: grief transformed into beginning.
